# Incident report: checkout failures from tax_engine_v2 rollout

**Date:** 2026-11-05
**Severity:** SEV1 (checkout-web 5xx peaked at 17.6%, above the 10% SEV1 threshold)
**Status:** Mitigated. Metrics confirm recovery. Follow-up work is open with payments and tax-platform.

## Timeline (UTC)
- 13:15: config change cfg_0412 on tax-service raised the DB connection pool from 50 to 80 (by jsato). Not linked to the errors; see Follow-ups.
- 13:41: deploy dep_7781, payments-api v2.13.4 → v2.14.0. No errors followed; not the cause.
- 14:02: feature flag flg_2210 (release-train) ramped `tax_engine_v2` from 10% to 100% on payments-api. First TaxEngineV2 timeouts on tax-service `/v2/quote` appear in payments-api logs at 14:02:31.
- 14:03: payments-api p99 jumps from 420 ms to 3150 ms. checkout-web and payments-api error rates jump from about 0.3% to 17.6% and 18.3%. tax-service logs "/v2/quote p99 3021ms; shedding load".
- 14:05: deploy dep_7790, search-api v5.2.0 → v5.2.1. search-api error rate stayed at 0.1%; its p95 warning (alt_33) started at 14:09. Not linked to checkout.
- 14:06: checkout-web 5xx alert fires (alt_32). payments-api p99 alert fired at 14:03 (alt_31).
- 14:08: tax-service logs "/v2/quote worker pool exhausted".
- 14:21: incident response started. Severity set to SEV1.
- 14:25: tax_engine_v2 rollout reverted from 100% to 10% (previous value) on payments-api.
- 14:29: status page updated to "identified".
- 14:30–14:31: checkout-web error rate falls to 0.4%. payments-api error rate falls to 0.3%. payments-api p99 falls to 450 ms.
- 14:36: status page updated to "mitigated".

## Root cause
The `tax_engine_v2` ramp from 10% to 100% (change **flg_2210**, 14:02 UTC) sent all checkout traffic through TaxEngineV2. That path calls tax-service `/v2/quote`. The tax service could not absorb the load: its worker pool was exhausted and it started shedding requests. payments-api `/charge` then returned 502 "tax quote unavailable", and checkout-web 5xx rose to 17.6%.

The timing lines up with the flag change, and the payments-api logs (TaxEngineV2 timeouts) and tax-service logs (load shedding, pool exhaustion) match it. The deploys at 13:41 and 14:05 and the tax-service config change at 13:15 do not match the onset, so they are not treated as the cause.

## Mitigation
Set `tax_engine_v2` rollout back to 10% (the previous value) via the feature flag. The flag is the least risky lever, so no deploy rollback was done. Effective in about 2 minutes.

## Verification
- checkout-web error rate: 17.6% → 0.4% (at 14:30), 0.4% at 14:30 is the last reading in the 5-minute window.
- payments-api error rate: 18.3% → 0.3% (at 14:31 onward).
- payments-api p99: 3150 ms → 450 ms (at 14:31 onward; baseline 420 ms).

Both error rates are under 1%, the runbook threshold for calling the incident mitigated. Verified recovery: **yes**. The flag has only been at 10% for a few minutes, so the customer impact of the 10% state should still be watched.

## Paging
- **payments** (payments-api owner), high urgency: notified of the cause and the flag revert, asked to own the tax_engine_v2 follow-up.
- **tax-platform** (tax-service owner), high urgency: notified of the load spike and pool exhaustion, asked to check /v2/quote capacity. (My first attempt used the team name "tax-service", which was rejected. I retried with the owning team, tax-platform.)
- **discovery**, low urgency: informed about the separate search-api p95 warning (alt_33). Not part of the checkout incident. search-api error rate is 0.1%.
- **security**: not paged. No credentials or secrets appeared in the logs I read.

## Status page
- 14:29 (identified): "Checkout errors for some customers"
- 14:36 (mitigated): same title, recovery stated.

## Follow-ups
1. payments / storefront: do not re-ramp `tax_engine_v2` until tax-service `/v2/quote` has capacity for 100% of checkout traffic. Add a canary or load test before the next ramp.
2. tax-platform: find out why `/v2/quote` saturated. Check whether the 13:15 pool change (cfg_0412, 50 → 80) interacted with this, and confirm the service is healthy now. I did not query tax-service metrics directly, so its recovery is unverified by me.
3. discovery: investigate the search-api p95 latency warning (alt_33), which started after dep_7790. Not related to checkout.
4. Release process: the release-train flag ramp went from 10% to 100% in one step with no guard on a downstream dependency.
